How to read this prototype · methods and sources

A temperament mapping is kept separate from generator tuning and the finite scale. The selected temperament uses one period and one generator. Commas determine how many periods make up the tempered reference interval (the first basis prime). This can be a full octave, a divided octave, or a non-octave reference such as 3/1 for a 3.5.7 basis. [19] means nineteen notes per period, not necessarily 19edo. Modes rotate the pitch-sorted scale and move its tonic to zero.

Published CWE tunings and preset mappings come from Xenharmonic Wiki’s meantone-family data. The mapping rows shown here use a reduced fifth rather than a twelfth generator. The 5-limit Porcupine, Magic and Hanson kernels are referenced in the 5-limit temperament catalog and the porcupine description; their initial tunings are computed prime least squares, not published CWE. 11-limit Porcupine uses the conventional tempered 11/10 generator and the published WE/CWE values from the porcupine-family data. Its WE reference uses a 1198.3250-cent period and a 162.5202-cent generator; The default CWE uses a pure octave and a 162.8156-cent generator. Published WE/CWE remain rounded reference presets. Computed WE/CWE solve the dual Weil–Euclidean quadratic objective directly from the mapping, for any supported prime basis, without looking up tuning values. For normalized prime errors z_i = cents_error_i / log2(prime_i), the objective is sum(z_i²) − sum(z_i)²/(d+1), with d basis primes. Computed WE fits both period and generator; computed CWE fixes the first basis prime pure, dividing its cents value by the number of periods. For an octave-based mapping this keeps 2/1 pure. See the WE metric definition and constrained tuning. Comma generation defaults to computed CWE; catalog matching chooses a familiar generator basis but the tuning is recalculated. Dreamtone uses 2.3.5.11.13; it does not map 7. Its 5-limit mapping matches meantone.

The tuning selector offers Weil–Euclidean, Minimax, Least Squares, EDO, and JI Target. Optimize period is off by default, keeping the mapping-derived reference period pure. Enabling it fits the period and generator together. EDO keeps its octave pure. The tuning panel offers minimax (smallest maximum absolute cents error) and least squares (smallest sum of squared cents errors). Targets are equally weighted. Basis-prime, mapped odd-limit, and custom target lists are available. The period may be fixed or fitted within half to twice the pure-reference period, with generator constrained strictly between 0 and the period. JI Target combines pure interval constraints with explicit coordinate assignments and mapping compatibility. With a free period and one independent exact target, WE selects among pure solutions. Incompatible targets are rejected. The EDO picker searches 2 through the chosen maximum (up to 5000) for integer period and generator steps whose induced val matches the patent val. Divided-octave periods require an integer step count per period. If 2 is in the basis, its EDO mapping is always exactly the EDO size. Optional nearby non-patent vals may differ from it by at most one step per basis prime. All listed induced vals factor through the selected temperament mapping and therefore annihilate its entire comma kernel. This is a bounded search, not a list of every possible non-patent val. Selecting a tuning method or changing its options retunes immediately. Minimax and Least Squares default to basis-prime targets. Least Squares with these targets minimizes equally weighted squared cents errors over the basis primes. This differs from the Weil–Euclidean metric. Manual tuning preserves the abstract mapping even at equal-step or pitch-collision boundaries.

MOS detection counts adjacent step sizes, including the closing step, at a tolerance of 0.00001 cents. Up to 256 notes are listed. A retained size that is no longer a MOS is marked as a generator stack. Ascending rows start at 0 cents and end with the period in parentheses. The left axis gives each starting note in cents; columns count steps upward from that note. Matrix intervals ascend within the selected matrix span.

Matrix JI targets come from the selected odd-limit diamond, plus 1/1, 2/1, and the reference prime interval. Targets retain their actual cents values; they are not folded into the displayed period. A mapped target beyond this period can therefore be absent from the finite scale. M identifies a target whose period and generator coordinates equal those of the displayed interval; its cell color reflects absolute cents error. A identifies an alternative approximation at other coordinates; O identifies a ratio outside the selected subgroup when the cell has no mapped hit. Multiple targets can appear in one cell. Tolerance updates automatically to the largest absolute error among mapped targets and the selected approximation source for the current limits and temperament. Blank target cells have no matches under the current filters. JI-target rows show the closest available approximations for every selected odd-limit target, including all equally close options and outside-subgroup targets. A mapped interval that is not among the best available options appears as a secondary comparison, with absent intervals labelled. Coverage counts report all mapped and other hits within tolerance, independently of this ranking. EDO-induced extra equivalences do not count as abstract mapped occurrences. Targets outside the temperament basis are marked unmapped.

JI Target lets you select any positive integer ratio and tune chosen integer period/generator coordinates pure. Its compatibility check preserves the current mapping and uses exact rational elimination to test additional assignments. A fully determined integer extension can be adopted without retuning. Incomplete extensions are marked unresolved; primes above 97 cannot be adopted in this prototype. Closest-alternative counts refer only to the finite scale, with coordinate identity retained even at EDO tunings. See consistency and Erlich’s discussion of consistency.

Discover → Chords uses the board-independent harmonic catalogue: mapped JI chords, JI intervals, essentially tempered shapes, compatible mapping alternatives, and better approximations. Exact ratio lookups retain spelling, repeated voices and registers. Scale filters compare the independent Discover and Play scales; a mapped harmony can remain available even when absent from either scale or above the tuning tolerance.

In B, select a harmony, choose an occurrence and voicing, then send its sounding coordinates to Play. Play preserves the requested scale and voices. Fit Play scale is an explicit action; a physical fingering is a separate choice. Reciprocal and octave-family links retain exact interpretations. ET searches start explicitly and report their bounds, target-set-relative evidence and unknown results. Mapping alternatives are previews until explicitly adopted; incidental approximations do not alter the canonical mapping. Diamond transfers retain cell provenance and sounding coordinates, including alternative approximations. Sessions preserve the selected harmony and optional material provenance; older session files still load with harmonic discovery enabled. See dyadic chords and Scala’s chord search prior art.

Play the HexBoard or tonality diamond with click, hold and drag. Shift sustains notes; Escape stops playback. Computer keyboard note playing is disabled. Session files preserve your temperament, layouts, and selected saved presets. Comma search is available under Advanced temperament search in Discover. Scala exports contain one period of pitches; no MIDI keyboard mapping is included.

Interface reference: Scale Workshop interval matrix. Prototype scope: rank 2, twenty built-in presets, saved personal presets, custom prime-basis mappings, and comma-list generation with exact rational elimination. Comma input must leave rank 2 and preserve the first basis prime. Integer mapping construction automatically derives the required period subdivision. Try 128/125 on 2.3.5 for three periods per octave, 2048/2025 for two, or 245/243 on 3.5.7 for a 3/1 reference. CWE makes these periods pure; WE can stretch them. Scale sizes, chords, and Scala exports cover one period. For divided-octave mappings, each matrix offers One period or Whole octave: the latter repeats the selected scale through all periods of the tempered octave, retaining generator coordinates and all JI target classifications. Stretched octaves keep their tuned size rather than being forced to 1200 cents. Large matrices have row and column paging. Arbitrary user-selected composite reference intervals and higher-rank scale enumeration are not supported yet.

HexBoard layout method and references. Each key stores integer period/generator coordinates. The base MOS’s adjacent large and small steps define the axes. Only target members play by default; an EDO pitch alias may occupy another coordinate and is labelled in the inspector. With period wrapping, interval overlays compare degrees modulo the actual temperament period, and chord placements retain their voiced period/generator coordinates. Without wrapping, interval overlays ascend within the tempered octave when it contains an integer number of periods; otherwise they ascend within one period. Board-edge omissions are reported before export.

Bosanquet and isomorphic layouts · Milne, Sethares & Plamondon: temperament layouts · HexBoard export protocol

Harmonic chord assessment

Harmonic discovery separates mapped intervals, tuning accuracy, scale occurrences and HexBoard fingerings. The manual inspector and board finder use the same interval and coherent-JI-lift services. Essentially tempered means every pair is mapped but no coherent JI chord exists within the selected target set; an incomplete assessment is shown as unknown. Search bounds and partial results are disclosed. The classic view and older session pins remain compatible.
